what: Plan does not require the LAUNCHER_FAILURE_CLASS and LAUNCHER_FAILURE_REASON token grammar to be enumerated identically in the launcher and ship-pr sibling contracts
scenario_or_breakage: An implementer can update lib-external-launcher-common.md with the full enum but leave launch-cursor-ci.md launch-codex-ci.md launch-claude-ci.md or ship-pr.md with only a vague "new KVs" mention, making later drift invisible to doc readers and review tooling
suggested_fix: Revise the plan to require either the exact literal grammar block in every listed sibling contract or a single canonical lib contract plus explicit "do not re-enumerate; pass through this grammar" references from every launcher and ship-pr.md

what: Planned token-pinning tests are incomplete and internally inconsistent for reason literals
scenario_or_breakage: The enum includes parse and no-action, but the test strategy says parse-error and never names no-action as a required emitted reason; a future rename or omission of no-action could pass behavior tests silently
suggested_fix: Revise the test plan to add a table-driven exact enum assertion for class tokens none health other and reason tokens auth binary-missing health-probe timeout parse no-action refusal unknown, plus one fixture that emits each literal

what: ship-pr guard parse logic is described by reference but not pinned as an exact anchored awk contract
scenario_or_breakage: The fail file is mixed launcher output; an implementer could use an unanchored grep/cut parser or parse the wrong assignment shape, causing explicit other to be missed or diagnostic text to trigger the bail path
suggested_fix: Add the exact snippets to the plan: launcher_failure_class=$(awk -F= '/^LAUNCHER_FAILURE_CLASS=/ {print $2; exit}' "$fail_file") and launcher_failure_reason=$(awk -F= '/^LAUNCHER_FAILURE_REASON=/ {print $2; exit}' "$fail_file"), followed by a case that bails only on other and treats health none empty and * as fall-through
